"

Timing your contractions

A contraction is the tightening of the uterine muscles. Women experience contractions in all kinds of ways, ranging from cramping to tightening, burning, backache, and more.

When you’re in true labour, contractions get progressively longer, stronger, more painful, and closer together.

Our contraction timer will help you keep track of what you’re experiencing. When a contraction begins, press “Start contraction,” and when it ends, press “Stop contraction.” We’ll record the info for you and calculate the length of your contractions and the time between them – and the averages, too.

Typically, when you’re having your first baby, your doctor or midwife will want you to call once you’ve spent at least one hour having contractions that come five minutes apart and last one minute each. But your doctor or midwife might have different instructions for you, so discuss the plan ahead of time.

Keep in mind that if your water breaks during the early part of labour, things may progress quickly from there. Notify your doctor, nurse, or midwife right away.

If this isn’t your first baby, you’ve experienced a fast labour before, or you’re already somewhat dilated and effaced, you may need to notify your doctor as soon as you begin to have painful contractions."
